answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like pigment sealed into a mesa wall: one identity, one deposit, no sharing. A bridge verifier then checks that each stake came from a distinct funding source and has aged for a fixed waiting period before granting any reputation weight. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore lock a thousand separate stakes and wait out the aging window for each one, so forgery cost grows linearly with every sockpuppet, while an honest agent pays only once and recovers its stake when it leaves.
